question: If secA + tanA = p, then what is secA in terms of p?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By standard trigonometric identity, if secA + tanA = p, then secA − tanA = 1/p.

Adding these two equations gives:

⇒ 2secA = p + 1/p

⇒ 2secA = (p² + 1)/p

⇒ secA = (p² + 1)/2p

**∴ The correct answer is (p² + 1)/2p.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

secA + tanA = p

**Formula Used:**

sec²A − tan²A = 1

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (secA − tanA)(secA + tanA) = 1

Substitute secA + tanA = p in the above equation:

⇒ (secA − tanA) × p = 1

⇒ secA − tanA = 1/p

Adding this result to the given equation (secA + tanA = p):

⇒ (secA + tanA) + (secA − tanA) = p + 1/p

⇒ 2secA = (p² + 1)/p

⇒ secA = (p² + 1)/2p

**∴ The correct answer is (p² + 1)/2p.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent Calculation

By subtracting the two equations, tanA = (p² − 1)/2p.

Sine Calculation

Since sinA = tanA ÷ secA, sinA = (p² − 1)/(p² + 1).

Cosecant and Cotangent Relation

Similarly, if cosecA + cotA = q, then cosecA − cotA = 1/q, yielding cosecA = (q² + 1)/2q.
